messages:
maya: Heads-up — I sketched a tiny proposal for per-route privacy_flags that control both telemetry sampling and inspect-mode visibility. Want quick feedback before I spin an RFC. TL;DR: a 3-bit flag per route: log_level, inspect_exempt, consent_scope.

tony: short Q: how does this interact with quotas? if inspect is on does it bump a different quota bucket? :thinking:

maya: good call — plan is quota-aware backpressure: inspect-mode traffic increments an `inspect_tokens` accounting counter separate from regular telemetry. routes can opt into 'inspect_shared' to tax the same quota though.

samir: can we avoid new quota explosions? maybe only allow inspect on routes with `rate_limit <= 50rps` by default, can request exceptions.

linh: redaction concern: we need clear defaults. If `inspect_exempt=false` we still store minimal metadata (route, anonymized client id, timestamp). If `inspect_exempt=true` we never persist payloads, only aggregate metrics.

jess: UX note — console needs a diff view for when a route flips privacy_flags. Users should see: before/after sampling rate, sample types (prefix/full), and any active redaction transforms. :eyes:

maya: agreed on diff. also want a small preview that shows an example sanitized payload (not real data) so SREs can confirm transforms without viewing live PII.

linh: on transforms — prefer pseudonymization (salted hashing) for user identifiers vs full redaction. but hashing needs salt rotation plan + access controls. we should treat salted hashes as PII if salts are reversible.

samir: propose scheme: two redaction levels — `mask` (replace with fixed token), `hash` (hmac with route-scoped salt). store policy metadata: `redaction_level: mask|hash|none` per field path.

maya: here's a tiny config example I put in the spec: ```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "privacy_flags": {"log_level": "sampled", "inspect_exempt": false, "consent_scope": "session"},
  "redaction": [{"path": "$.user.email","level":"hash"},{"path":"$.prompt","level":"mask"}]
}
```

tony: nit: need to handle multi-part forms & binary attachments — our redactors today are text-first. either reject inspect for binary or provide a safe containerization step.

jess: also add telemetry counters: `pii_incident_attempts`, `inspect_view_grants`, and `route_pseudonymized_count`. must surface in console with clear TTL windows.

maya: rollout plan idea — feature-flag the privacy_flags wire first (no-op), then UI toggle in console -> 10% route canaries -> 100% with auto-audit capturing delta metrics. ops-bot can automate the canary and alert on PII_incident_attempts spike.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure KMS access for salt store, bind `inspect_view` to RBAC group, enable audit-log retention 90d.

linh: encryption & key rotation: we must rotate salts with overlap window and mark historical hashes as epoch-tagged. lookup must try current salt then previous N salts. document migration cost.

samir: performance: hashed fields add CPU. suggest we only hash at ingest for sampled telemetry, and for high-throughput routes prefer `mask`. add a compile-time warning in planner when route throughput > threshold and `hash` is selected.

jess: one more UX ask — console should show effective sampling probability (computed from route settings + global quotas) and allow temporary 'inspect-preview' for owners only (TTL=1h).

maya: great, I'll add these to the spec and include an example rollout feature-flag snippet for infra. ping me if you want to be a reviewer. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary job scheduled: privacy-flags-canary v0.1 -> 10 routes -> 24h metrics window.

tony: +1 to reviewing. can we also include an emergency 'breakglass' that allows on-call to temporarily enable inspect for a single request id with audit trail?

linh: breakglass ok if it's gated by an approval flow and generates a signed justification entry stored in audit logs. no ad-hoc console toggles.

maya: noted — will add breakglass flow w/ signed justification + auto-revoke TTL. thanks all, I'll open the RFC and link here. :rocket:
